Recommended Highlights This Week

1. FIFA World Cup 2026 – Round of 32 concludes, Round of 16 begins

2. Singapore International Piano Festival – 2–5 July

3. A Magical Island Adventure at Sentosa – new Disney Cruise Line takeover

4. TwoSet Violin World Tour with the SSO – 2 & 3 July

5. Milli: Sky Dining, Bar & Lounge – new rooftop opening

6. Juju World Singapore – continues at Gardens by the Bay

Overall Summary

Football fever remains the backdrop to the week as the FIFA World Cup moves from the Round of 32 into the Round of 16, with Lau Pa Sat and CHIJMES still packed for late-night screenings. On Sentosa, Disney's cruise takeover brings character meet-and-greets and evening lighting to Palawan Beach, while classical music fans have two very different options – the Singapore International Piano Festival and a rather unusual SSO collaboration with YouTube violin duo TwoSet. On the dining front, National Gallery Singapore's rooftop finally opens as Milli: Sky Dining, Bar & Lounge.

Events & Festivals

FIFA World Cup 2026 – Round of 32 & Round of 16

The knockout stage continues across the US, Canada and Mexico. Lau Pa Sat and the CHIJMES/Capitol Singapore fan zones remain the best places in town to catch the action on big screens, running through 20 July.

Round of 32 concludes: through 3 July

- Mon 29 June: Brazil 2-1 Japan; Netherlands 1-1 Morocco (Morocco won on penalties)

- Wed 1 July: England 2-1 DR Congo; Belgium 3-2 Senegal (AET); USA 2-0 Bosnia

- Thu 2 July: Spain 3-0 Austria; Portugal 2-1 Croatia

Round of 16 begins:

- Sat 4 July: Canada v Morocco, Houston – kickoff 1:00am Sunday SGT

- Sat 4 July: Paraguay v France, Philadelphia – kickoff 5:00am Sunday SGT

- Sun 5 July: Brazil v Norway, New Jersey – kickoff 4:00am Monday SGT

Location: Lau Pa Sat / CHIJMES / Capitol Singapore (public fan zones)

Concierge Recommendation: Screens fill up fast for marquee fixtures – guests wanting a seat for the England or Brazil matches should be advised to arrive at least 45 minutes before kickoff.

Singapore International Piano Festival

The annual festival returns, showcasing pianists and composers across an intimate programme of recitals.

Event Date: 2–5 July 2026

Best For: Couples / Classical Music Lovers / Culture Seekers

Concierge Recommendation: A refined alternative for guests looking for something quieter than the football crowds this week.

Attractions & Activities

A Magical Island Adventure at Sentosa

Sentosa's new Disney Cruise Line collaboration takes over Palawan Beach, San Fransokyo Street, Toy Story Place and Marvel Landing, with character meet-and-greets and the Southernmost Point lit up after dark. Disney Adventure Cruise guests sailing between 24 June and 1 October also enjoy complimentary access to one Sentosa attraction.

Event Date: From 24 June 2026, until 20 September 2026

Character Meet Dates: 27–28 June, 18–19 July, 15–16 August (3pm, 4pm, 5:30pm, 6:30pm)

Location: Sentosa

Best For: Families / Disney Fans / Cruise Guests

Concierge Recommendation: New this week – worth flagging to any family guests, especially those who've booked a Disney Adventure Cruise sailing, since the complimentary attraction access is easy to miss if they don't ask.

Juju World Singapore

Australian artist CJ Hendry's larger-than-life inflatable playground, built around her collectible Juju bunny character, continues at IMBA Theatre – a world premiere for an exclusive yellow Juju colourway found only in Singapore.

Event Date: 20 June–18 July 2026

Location: IMBA Theatre, Gardens by the Bay

Best For: Families / Young Adults / Instagram-Friendly / Collectors

Concierge Recommendation: A fun, colourful stop for families with young children, and popular with guests chasing the exclusive Singapore-only merchandise.

Restaurants & Bars

Milli: Sky Dining, Bar & Lounge

The long-awaited rooftop addition to National Gallery Singapore has opened, taking over the former Smoke & Mirrors space. Chef LG Han of Michelin-starred Labyrinth teams up with Vijay Mudaliar of Native and the team behind nightlife concept Bae's Cocktail Club for a two-storey rooftop restaurant and club lounge.

Location: 1 St Andrew's Road, #05-02/#06-01, National Gallery Singapore

Signature Dishes: Spring chicken rice paella; king crab with white pepper and salted egg yolk sauce

Best For: Couples / Business Travellers / Skyline Views

Concierge Recommendation: A strong new addition to recommend for an evening out – suggest arriving before sunset to catch the transition from daylight to skyline views.

Hikiniku to Come

The cult-favourite Tokyo charcoal-grilled hamburg steak chain has made its Singapore debut at VivoCity. The concept is deliberately simple – a single set meal of three 90g patties, ground fresh in-store and grilled over binchotan charcoal, served one at a time so each arrives sizzling hot.

Location: VivoCity

Price: Set meal from S$27.90++

Best For: Solo Diners / Japanese Cuisine Fans / Quick Lunch

Concierge Recommendation: Expect queues – this one's been hyped since its Tokyo days. Best for guests happy to wait, or advise an early lunch before the noon rush.

Seoul & So

National Gallery Singapore's newest tenant serves hanwoo tasting courses alongside lunch sets and a la carte Korean dishes, from Seoul galbi to gwangyang bulgogi.

Location: #05-03, National Gallery Singapore, 1 St Andrew's Road

Opening Hours: Daily, 12:00pm–3:00pm & 6:00pm–10:30pm

Price: Hanwoo tasting course S$119; lunch sets from S$45

Best For: Couples / Korean Cuisine Lovers / Civic District Guests

Concierge Recommendation: Pairs naturally with a Milli nightcap in the same building – a good full-evening recommendation for guests exploring the Civic District.

Concerts, Theatre & Entertainment

TwoSet Violin World Tour

Australian-Taiwanese classical violin duo Brett Yang and Eddy Chen – known for blending comedy, livestreams and serious musicianship – bring their world tour to Singapore for two nights, joined by the Singapore Symphony Orchestra under conductor Joshua Tan.

Event Date: 2 & 3 July 2026

Best For: Classical Music Fans / Young Adults / TwoSet Followers

Concierge Recommendation: A great crossover pick for guests who enjoy classical music but want something livelier than a standard concert hall evening.

Hotel & Hospitality News

NoMad Singapore

Hilton's NoMad Singapore is on track for a late 2026 opening on Orchard Road. The 19-storey hotel will house three dining and bar concepts – NoMad Grill, a New York-style chophouse; The Tropicana Club, a cabaret-inspired cocktail bar; and Sticky Fingers, a soft-serve and cocktail concept – plus a rooftop pool lounge.

Address: 230 Orchard Rd, Singapore 238854

General Manager: Bernardo de la Garza – 18 years in luxury and lifestyle hospitality across Six Senses, Hyatt and Accor; most recently GM at The Standard, Bangkok Mahanakhon

Director of Culinary: Lorenz Hoja – has cooked across England, France, Austria, the Maldives and Singapore, including over a decade in Joel Robuchon's kitchens

ATLAS

One of Singapore's most iconic Art Deco bars, tucked inside Parkview Square, with one of the largest gin collections in the world.

Cuisine: Cocktails & European Dining

Location: Parkview Square

Dress Code: Smart Casual

Website: https://atlasbar.sg

Best For: Couples / Business Travellers / Luxury Travellers / Nightlife

Concierge Recommendation: A dependable premium evening pick. Book ahead for Friday and Saturday.

MENSHO X

The celebrated Tokyo ramen brand's first outlet outside Japan has opened at Raffles Place. Expect inventive flavours, lighter broths and housemade noodles, including the Mochi Mochi Mazemen and a Toripaitan Tsukemen with yuzu.

Location: 6 Battery Road, #01-02, Singapore 049909

Best For: Ramen Enthusiasts / Business Travellers / Solo Diners

Concierge Recommendation: Great lunch pick for guests staying near Raffles Place – expect queues at peak hours, so suggest an off-peak visit.

Transport & Operational Updates

FIFA Fan Zone Crowds

Expect heavier footfall and later closing hours around Lau Pa Sat, CHIJMES and Capitol Singapore through 20 July as fan zone screenings continue into the early hours for US-timezone kickoffs.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Mid-year travel season traffic remains high. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

SimplyGo Public Transport

Contactless Visa, Mastercard, Amex or NETS cards work directly on the MRT and buses – no separate transport card required.

Looking Ahead

FIFA World Cup 2026 – Round of 16 Continues

Round of 16 fixtures continue through 7 July, with the Quarterfinals following from 9–11 July. Expect fan zone crowds to build further as the tournament narrows.

Concierge Recommendation: Guests wanting a guaranteed seat for the bigger fixtures should be advised to arrive well ahead of kickoff, particularly for matches involving England, Brazil, France or Argentina.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Fan zones at Lau Pa Sat and CHIJMES will be busiest during evening and early-morning kickoffs – flag this for guests planning a late dinner nearby.

  • Milli and Seoul & So are both newly opened in the same building – easy to combine into one Civic District evening.

Sentosa Family Time

A Magical Island Adventure - character meet-and-greet - Southernmost Point evening lighting

Full Day

Civic District & Dining

National Gallery Singapore - Seoul & So lunch - Milli: Sky Dining, Bar & Lounge nightcap

2 Days

Day 1

Gardens by the Bay - Juju World Singapore - MENSHO X dinner at Raffles Place

Day 2

FIFA fan zone at Lau Pa Sat - ATLAS nightcap

Best New Restaurant: Milli: Sky Dining, Bar & Lounge

Best Free Fan Experience: FIFA Fan Zones at Lau Pa Sat & CHIJMES

2. The Portals Experience – new immersive exhibition

Overall Summary

The World Cup narrows further this week as the Round of 16 wraps up and the Quarterfinals begin, with several co-host nations already eliminated – expect fan zone energy to stay high right through the weekend. On Sentosa and at Scotts Road, two new immersive experiences open their doors: CRYBABY's giant inflatable sea creatures at Resorts World Sentosa, and The Portals Experience, a fantasy and sci-fi walkthrough near Orchard. On the transport side, note that Downtown Line Friday night early closures begin this week and will run for several weeks.

Events & Festivals

FIFA World Cup 2026 – Round of 16 & Quarterfinals

The Round of 16 concludes this week with several upsets, including Norway's shock win over five-time champions Brazil, before the Quarterfinals begin on the 9th.

Round of 16 (concludes):

- Mon 6 July: Spain 1-0 Portugal, Dallas – kickoff 3:00am SGT (7 July)

- Mon 6 July: Belgium 4-1 USA, Seattle – kickoff 8:00am SGT (7 July)

- Tue 7 July: Argentina 3-2 Egypt, Atlanta

Quarterfinals begin:

- Thu 9 July: France 2-0 Morocco, Boston

- Fri 10 July: Spain 2-1 Belgium, Los Angeles

- Sat 11 July: England 2-1 Norway (AET), Miami; Argentina 3-1 Switzerland (AET), Kansas City

Location: Lau Pa Sat / CHIJMES / Capitol Singapore (public fan zones)

Concierge Recommendation: Semifinal spots are now on the line – expect the loudest crowds of the tournament so far for the Argentina and England fixtures this weekend.

Attractions & Activities

The Portals Experience

A new fantasy and sci-fi immersive experience opens near Orchard, built around original artworks, themed realms, miniatures and interactive displays.

Event Date: Opens this week, until 2 September 2026

Time: 9:00am–9:00pm, last entry 8:00pm

Location: Fever Exhibition Hall, 25 Scotts Road

Admission: From S$26 for adults and S$17 for children

Website: https://portals-experience.sg/

Recommended Duration: 60–90 minutes

Best For: Families / Sci-Fi Fans / Fantasy Fans / Orchard Area Guests

Concierge Recommendation: A handy new option for guests based near Orchard, especially useful on a rainy afternoon.

CRYBABY at Resorts World Sentosa

Three five-metre inflatable sculptures – an anglerfish, a pufferfish and a whale shark – have gone on display across RWS, alongside a CRYBABY pop-up store near the Coach Singapore boutique.

Event Date: This week, until 30 August 2026

Location: Resorts World Sentosa

Best For: Families / Young Adults / Collectors / Photography

Concierge Recommendation: A fun, free add-on for anyone already spending the day at RWS – great for photos.

Restaurants & Bars

Bibim Deli

Culinary Class Wars season one chef Yohan Kim has opened this economical Korean DIY rice bowl concept, letting diners mix and match more than 20 rotating banchan and sauces onto a free base bowl of rice.

Best For: Solo Diners / Casual Lunch / Korean Cuisine Fans / Budget-Conscious Guests

Concierge Recommendation: A good value lunch recommendation for guests wanting something quick and casual between meetings.

Sukiyaki Jin

Singapore's first A5 wagyu tomato sukiyaki has arrived in Orchard, putting a tomato-based twist on the traditional hot pot.

Location: Orchard

Best For: Couples / Japanese Cuisine Fans / Special Occasions

Concierge Recommendation: A distinctive dinner pick for guests who've already tried the more familiar sukiyaki spots and want something different.

Hotel & Hospitality News

Pan Pacific Hotels Group – Cluster GM Appointment

Pan Pacific Hotels Group has appointed Kung Teong Wah as cluster general manager overseeing both Parkroyal Collection Pickering, Singapore and Parkroyal on Beach Road, Singapore, expanding his existing role at Parkroyal Collection Pickering.

General Manager: Kung Teong Wah – more than three decades of hospitality experience, with deep expertise in Singapore's hotel sector; previously General Manager of Parkroyal on Beach Road

Transport & Operational Updates

Downtown Line Night Works – Begins This Week

From 10 July, trains on the entire Downtown Line end at 11:30pm on Friday nights and resume at 8:30am on Saturdays, continuing over several weeks while systems testing is carried out. Shuttle buses cover the gap.

FIFA Fan Zone Crowds

Quarterfinal weekend (9–11 July) will bring heavier footfall and later closing hours around Lau Pa Sat, CHIJMES and Capitol Singapore.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Mid-year travel season traffic remains high. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

Looking Ahead

FIFA World Cup 2026 – Semifinals

Semifinals are set for 14 and 15 July: France v Spain and England v Argentina. Expect this to be the busiest fan zone weekend of the tournament so far.

Concierge Recommendation: Guests should be advised to book fan zone seating or arrive well ahead of kickoff for the semifinals – these are expected to draw the largest crowds yet.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Downtown Line Friday night early closures begin this week – flag this for any guests with late Friday travel plans via the DTL.

  • CRYBABY and The Portals Experience both make good rainy-day or between-meetings additions for guests already in the RWS or Orchard areas.

Sentosa Family Time

A Magical Island Adventure - CRYBABY photo stops - Southernmost Point evening lighting

Full Day

Orchard & Civic District

The Portals Experience - Bibim Deli lunch - Seoul & So dinner at National Gallery

Recommended Highlights This Week

2. FIFA World Cup 2026 Semifinals – 14 & 15 July

3. Tiffany & Co. Blue Box Cafe – opens mid-July at ION Orchard

4. Exploria – new multimedia attraction at Mandai Wildlife Reserve

Overall Summary

This is the week it all comes down to: Semifinals on the 14th and 15th, the Bronze Final on the 18th, and the FIFA World Cup Final itself on the 19th – expect this to be the single busiest week for fan zone crowds across Lau Pa Sat, CHIJMES and Capitol Singapore. Also note that Juju World Singapore closes on the 18th, so this is last call for guests who haven't been yet. On the dining and hotel side, Tiffany's Blue Box Cafe finally opens at ION Orchard, and we're featuring two of Sentosa and Mandai's standout luxury stays this week – Raffles Sentosa Singapore and Mandai Rainforest Resort by Banyan Tree.

Events & Festivals

FIFA World Cup 2026 – Semifinals, Bronze Final & Final

The tournament reaches its climax this week. Spain beat France and Argentina beat England in the Semifinals to set up a Final rematch of the 2010 championship game.

Semifinals:

- Tue 14 July: Spain 2-0 France, Arlington – kickoff approx. 3am SGT (15 July)

- Wed 15 July: Argentina 2-1 England, Atlanta – kickoff approx. 6am SGT (16 July)

Third-Place Play-Off:

- Sat 18 July: France 4-6 England (on penalties), Miami

Final:

- Sun 19 July: Spain v Argentina, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford – kickoff 8:00pm BST, approx. 3:00am SGT (20 July)

Location: Lau Pa Sat / CHIJMES / Capitol Singapore (public fan zones)

Concierge Recommendation: This is the biggest fan zone night of the tournament – advise guests planning to watch the Final at Lau Pa Sat or CHIJMES to arrive well before midnight, as seating will go quickly ahead of the early-morning kickoff.

Attractions & Activities

Exploria

A new large-scale indoor nature-themed multimedia attraction has opened at Mandai Wildlife Reserve, taking guests through five immersive digital worlds – prehistoric, microscopic, deep-sea and extreme environments.

Location: Mandai Wildlife Reserve

Admission: Ticketed

Website: https://www.mandai.com/en/exploria.html

Recommended Duration: 1.5–3 hours

Best For: Families / Rainy Day / Young Adults

Concierge Recommendation: A great addition to pair with a Bird Paradise or Night Safari visit, and a strong rainy-day fallback.

Restaurants & Bars

Tiffany & Co. Blue Box Cafe

Tiffany's first-ever cafe concept in Southeast Asia opens this week at ION Orchard, on the top floor of the newly reopened flagship store. The menu is developed alongside Julien Royer of three-Michelin-starred Odette – American cafe classics with French polish and a few Singapore touches.

Location: ION Orchard

Best For: Couples / Luxury Travellers / Special Occasions

Concierge Recommendation: Expect tables to disappear fast – advise guests to book as early as possible, ideally as soon as reservations open.

Hotel & Hospitality News

Raffles Sentosa Singapore

Singapore's first all-villa Raffles resort, featured this week for its private pool villas, destination dining and wellness offering.

Website: https://www.raffles.com/sentosa/

Cluster General Manager: Cavaliere Giovanni Viterale (also overseeing Sofitel Singapore Sentosa Resort & Spa) – 36 years in hospitality, formerly General Manager of The Fullerton Hotels and Resorts

Best For: Luxury Travellers / Honeymooners / Couples

Concierge Recommendation: A great fit for guests wanting an exclusive staycation or a standout dining experience.

Mandai Rainforest Resort by Banyan Tree

A nature-inspired stay right inside Mandai Wildlife Reserve, featured this week as a strong base for exploring Singapore Zoo, Bird Paradise, Exploria and Night Safari.

Website: https://www.mandai.com/en/mandai-rainforest-resort-by-banyan-tree.html

General Manager: Michel Scheffers – over 25 years across luxury and lifestyle hospitality including ONYX Hospitality Group, Shangri-La and Hilton; took over from opening GM Glen Cook

Best For: Families / Nature Lovers / Couples

Concierge Recommendation: A strong pick for anyone planning a two-day wildlife itinerary, especially now that Exploria has opened right next door.

Transport & Operational Updates

FIFA Final Weekend Crowds

Expect the heaviest fan zone crowds of the tournament around Lau Pa Sat, CHIJMES and Capitol Singapore from 18–20 July, with early-morning kickoffs keeping venues open through the night.

Downtown Line Night Works

Trains on the entire Downtown Line continue ending at 11:30pm on Friday nights and resuming at 8:30am on Saturdays, while systems testing continues. Shuttle buses cover the gap.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Mid-year travel season traffic remains high. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

Looking Ahead

Post-World Cup Transition

With the Final on 19 July marking the close of the tournament, fan zone screenings at Lau Pa Sat and CHIJMES are expected to wind down shortly after. Upcoming editions will shift focus back to Singapore's regular events calendar.

Concierge Recommendation: This is the last week to point football-following guests toward the fan zones – make the most of the Final atmosphere while it lasts.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Juju World Singapore closes on the 18th – last chance to send families before it's gone.

  • The Final kicks off in the early hours of the 20th Singapore time – guests planning a fan zone night should be told this clearly to avoid confusion.

  • Tiffany & Co. Blue Box Cafe is walk-up only for now – confirm current booking policy with the venue directly before advising guests.

ION Orchard shopping - Tiffany & Co. Blue Box Cafe - Portals Experience

Full Day

Mandai Wildlife Day

Singapore Zoo - Exploria - Mandai Rainforest Resort by Banyan Tree lunch - Night Safari

Sentosa GrillFest prep - Raffles Sentosa Singapore staycation - CRYBABY photo stops

Overall Summary

Sentosa GrillFest opens on the 23rd and runs into mid-August, giving us a solid new beachfront recommendation. It's also a big week for K-pop, with EXO back in Singapore for the first time since 2019 and Mitski playing The Star Theatre. National Day prep steps up a gear too – the first public Preview is on the 25th, so expect Kallang to get busy. On the food side, MENSHO X has just landed at Raffles Place with its first-ever outlets outside Tokyo, which is worth flagging to anyone who loves ramen.

Events & Festivals

Sentosa GrillFest

Sentosa's beachfront cookout is back for its ninth year, and this time it's bringing 42 food vendors across five zones plus something new – Chef's Grill, an eight-course omakase-style dinner right on the sand.

Event Date: 23 July–16 August 2026 (selected Thu–Sun dates)

Time: 4:00pm–10:30pm

Location: Siloso Beach, Sentosa

Admission: Free entry; food and beverage purchased separately

Best For: Couples / Groups / Food Lovers / Sunset Diners

Concierge Recommendation: We can start recommending this one now that it's open. Tell guests to time their arrival for sunset – that's when it really comes alive. Chef's Grill has limited seats, so get guests to book ahead if they're keen.

F1 Exhibition Singapore

A new motorsport exhibition opens this week, walking visitors through the history and stories behind Formula One. Good timing, too – it's clearly building anticipation ahead of this year's Singapore Grand Prix.

Event Date: 23 July–2 August 2026

Best For: Formula One Fans / Families / Repeat Visitors

Concierge Recommendation: Pair this with the Singapore GP ALL ACCESS 2.0 experience at the F1 Pit Building – makes for a great full day out for any motorsport fan staying with us.

A Magical Island Adventure at Sentosa

Sentosa's Disney Cruise Line takeover is still going strong, with installations spread across Palawan Beach, San Fransokyo Street, Toy Story Place and Marvel Landing – think a six-metre inflatable anchor and a towering Baymax you really can't miss. The Southernmost Point now stays open till 10pm too, lit up as a glowing coastal escape after dark.

Event Date: Until 20 September 2026

Location: Sentosa

Website: https://www.sentosa.com.sg/en/campaigns/magicalislandadventure/

Recommended Duration: Half day

Best For: Families / Disney Fans / Cruise Guests / Sentosa Visitors

Concierge Recommendation: Still one of our go-to family recommendations. If guests can stay into the evening, the Southernmost Point lighting is worth planning the visit around.

CRYBABY at Resorts World Sentosa

Hard to miss these – five-metre inflatable sculptures of an anglerfish, a pufferfish and a whale shark have taken over RWS, alongside a CRYBABY pop-up store near the Coach Singapore boutique.

Event Date: Until 30 August 2026

Location: Resorts World Sentosa

Best For: Families / Young Adults / Collectors / Photography

Concierge Recommendation: Easy add-on for anyone already spending the day at RWS – free, quick, and great for photos.

Istana Open House – National Day

The Istana opened its grounds to the public on Sunday, 26 July, in celebration of National Day, including – for the first time at an Istana Open House – an evening outdoor concert on the lawns.

Event Date: 26 July 2026

Time: 9:30am–8:00pm (last entry 6:45pm)

Location: The Istana, Orchard Road (nearest MRT: Dhoby Ghaut)

Admission: Free for Singaporeans and PRs

Best For: Families / Heritage & Culture / Free Activities

Concierge Recommendation: This was a same-week, date-specific event tied to a public holiday period – worth building a habit of checking for Istana Open House dates each time a national holiday falls within an edition's window, so we don't miss flagging it to guests again.

Attractions & Activities

Faster Football Singapore

A fast-paced 7-a-side football tournament returns this week, bringing in club teams and players from some of the biggest leagues in the world for a condensed, high-energy format.

Event Date: 24–26 July 2026

Best For: Football Fans / Families / Groups

Concierge Recommendation: Good one for guests missing the World Cup buzz once it's over. Tickets may move fast given the timing right after the Final, so check availability early.

Explore Your Canon – Canon PhotoMarathon

Canon's biggest PhotoMarathon yet takes over Urban Park at Guoco Tower this week, with hands-on photography experiences and workshops for everyone from beginners to enthusiasts.

Event Date: 23–25 July 2026

Location: Urban Park @ Guoco Tower

Best For: Photography Enthusiasts / Young Adults

Concierge Recommendation: A nice niche pick for guests who are into photography. Worth checking whether on-site registration is needed before sending anyone down.

Exploria

One of the largest indoor nature-themed multimedia attractions in Southeast Asia, Exploria takes guests through five immersive digital worlds – prehistoric, microscopic, deep-sea and extreme environments.

Location: Mandai Wildlife Reserve

Admission: Ticketed

Website: https://www.mandai.com/en/exploria.html

Recommended Duration: 1.5–3 hours

Best For: Families / Rainy Day / Young Adults / Repeat Visitors

Concierge Recommendation: Great fallback for a rainy afternoon, and works well tacked onto a Bird Paradise or Night Safari visit.

The Portals Experience

A fantasy and sci-fi immersive experience built around original artworks, themed realms, miniatures and interactive displays – the kind of thing that photographs beautifully too.

Event Date: Until 2 September 2026

Time: 9:00am–9:00pm, last entry 8:00pm

Location: Fever Exhibition Hall, 25 Scotts Road

Admission: From S$26 for adults and S$17 for children

Website: https://portals-experience.sg/

Recommended Duration: 60–90 minutes

Best For: Families / Sci-Fi Fans / Fantasy Fans / Rainy Day / Orchard Area Guests

Concierge Recommendation: Handy one to have in your back pocket for guests based near Orchard, especially if it's raining or just too hot to be outside.

Restaurants & Bars

MENSHO X

This is a big one – the celebrated Tokyo ramen brand has opened its first outlets outside Japan, right here in Singapore. Expect inventive flavours, lighter broths and housemade noodles, including seasonal specials like the Mochi Mochi Mazemen and a Toripaitan Tsukemen with yuzu.

Opening: 14 July 2026

Location: 6 Battery Road, #01-02, Singapore 049909

Best For: Ramen Enthusiasts / Business Travellers / Solo Diners

Half Day – Sentosa Family Escape

Morning: Take the Sentosa Express or cable car over – the cable car ride itself is worth it for the harbour views, and doubles as the first “attraction” of the day.

Midday: Work through A Magical Island Adventure's character meet-and-greets across Palawan Beach and San Fransokyo Street.

Full Day – Civic District, Orchard & Dinner

Morning: Start at Merlion Park for the classic skyline photo, then walk through the Civic District past the Padang, City Hall and the old Supreme Court building (now National Gallery Singapore).

Midday: Explore the National Gallery itself, or continue on to Gardens by the Bay for the Supertrees and conservatories if guests prefer greenery over galleries.

Afternoon: Head to Orchard Road for shopping, then lunch or an early dinner at Bouillon Gavroche in Mandarin Gallery.

Evening: The Portals Experience on Scotts Road is a short walk from Mandarin Gallery and works well as an after-dinner stop; on 1 August specifically, swap this for Symphony in the Gardens at the Botanic Gardens instead.

Tip: This day covers two very different areas of town – Civic District and Orchard – so budget taxi or MRT time between the morning and afternoon halves rather than trying to walk it all.

2 Days – Marina Bay & Sentosa

Day 1 – Marina Bay & Chinatown

Morning: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark or the Helix Bridge for skyline views, then Gardens by the Bay.

Afternoon: Chinatown – the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Chinatown Street Market, and a wander down Ann Siang Hill.

Evening: Dinner at Bouillon Gavroche, then a stroll along Marina Bay to see the skyline lit up.

Day 2 – Sentosa Island

Morning to Afternoon: Sentosa GrillFest prep, A Magical Island Adventure, CRYBABY photo stops.

Evening: Stay for GrillFest dinner on Siloso Beach as the day winds down.

Tip: Book Sentosa GrillFest's Chef's Grill ahead if guests want a seat – it's the one part of this two-day plan that can't be improvised on the day.

Day 1: Orchard Road shopping and dining, capped with an evening at The Portals Experience or Bouillon Gavroche.

Day 2: Sentosa Island in full – GrillFest, Magical Island Adventure, CRYBABY – best done as a full day given how spread out the island is.

Day 3: Heritage morning through Kampong Glam (Sultan Mosque, Haji Lane) and Little India, followed by an evening built around whatever's on – NDP Preview 2 fireworks from Kallang Riverside Park on the 1st, or Symphony in the Gardens the same evening for a quieter alternative.

Hungry Ghost Festival – Background & Cultural Notes

The Hungry Ghost Festival (also known as Zhong Yuan Jie) falls during the seventh month of the Lunar calendar – 13 August to 10 September this year, with Ghost Day itself on 27 August. Tradition holds that the gates of the afterlife open on the first day of the seventh month, allowing spirits to roam the living world until the month ends. The festival blends Buddhist and Taoist traditions that developed in China over many centuries: the Buddhist Ullambana observance, centred on filial piety and easing the suffering of ancestors, merged over time with the Taoist Zhongyuan festival honouring wandering spirits with no living descendants to care for them. It's often compared to Mexico's Día de Muertos or North America's Halloween – a tradition of remembering and paying respect to the deceased, rather than something to be alarmed by.

During this period, guests may notice incense and joss paper burning near roadsides and void decks, small food offerings left in public areas, and getai (outdoor stage) performances with empty front-row seats reserved for spirits, by tradition. None of this affects transport or access, but a brief, respectful explanation helps guests understand what they're seeing rather than feel confused or alarmed by it.

Lilytopia

This is Gardens by the Bay's first-ever ancient Egypt-themed floral display, and it's worth knowing why it's not just “lilies you can find anywhere”: more than 7,000 lilies across 46 species and varieties fill the Flower Dome, anchored by a rare, genuinely significant bloom – the Egyptian Blue Lotus (Nymphaea caerulea), a sacred water lily that was so revered in ancient Egypt it was buried alongside pharaohs as a symbol of rebirth and the sun. It closes at night and reopens with the morning sun, the same cycle that made it a symbol of creation thousands of years ago. The display also marks the Flower Dome debut of two giant waterlily species, Victoria amazonica and Victoria cruziana – among the largest waterlilies in the world – grown from seed over 18 months by the Gardens’ own horticulture team. The centrepiece is a 4.5-metre-tall façade inspired by the Great Temple of Abu Simbel, with four colossal seated statues of Ramesses II, alongside figures of Egyptian deities including Hathor, Ra and Thoth.

Transport & Operational Updates

Road closures for the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix are in effect from 12:01am on Wednesday, 7 October until 5:30am on Tuesday, 13 October. Affected roads include Nicoll Highway, St Andrew's Road, Raffles Boulevard, Republic Boulevard, Raffles Avenue, Bayfront Avenue, Esplanade Drive, Stamford Road and Bras Basah Road. Selected stretches reopen briefly each morning (5:30am–10:00am) on 7, 8, 9 and 12 October. A single-lane Access Lane along Raffles Boulevard stays open via Nicoll Highway or Temasek Boulevard, except for buses and W, X and Y-plated vehicles; taxis and motorcycles can use it at all times except during track activity hours. Car parks at Suntec City, Millenia Walk and Marina Square remain open throughout.

Trains run later on race nights: the last trains from City Hall MRT leave at 12:30am on 9 and 10 October and 12:45am on 11 October. The nearest MRT stations to the circuit are City Hall, Esplanade, Promenade and Raffles Place. Expect heavy congestion across the city, not only around the circuit, and higher hotel rates and occupancy between 5 and 12 October.

Getting to the circuit: MRT is the recommended way to reach Marina Bay Street Circuit, with nine gates each within walking distance of a station – Gate 1 (Nicoll Highway), Gate 2 (Promenade), Gates 3A/3B (City Hall / Esplanade), Gates 4–6 (Raffles Place), Gate 7 (Esplanade), and Gate 8 (Bayfront). Guests heading to Gate 1 can also use Lavender MRT, which connects to the gate by a short dedicated shuttle service. For guests taking a taxi or private hire, the nearest official drop-off points are along Nicoll Highway for Gate 1; at Conrad Centennial, Pan Pacific Singapore or The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore for Gate 2; and at Marina Bay Sands for Gate 8 – all a short walk from the gate itself, since vehicles cannot approach the gates directly. Once inside the Circuit Park, race organisers also run a shuttle service between distant gates and zones – useful since Zone 1 (Pit, Turn 1–Turn 3) and Zone 4 (Padang, Esplanade Waterfront, Stamford) are a substantial walk apart; look for signage at each zone entrance.
